issues.display_title: Issue #1888: fix(payment): stop cc_purchase and invoice generation on subscription downgrade
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Fix phantom invoice record generation by completely removing cc_purchase insertion and invoice PDF generation during subscription downgrade across both Stripe and PayPal. Downgrade is a plan schedule update that does not charge the user immediately; billing will occur on the next cycle.

Closes #1887
Ref #1747, #1748, #1750

Background

  • Currently, DowngradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade() only skips cc_purchase insertion and invoice generation if $deferInvoice ($this->isTestMode) is true.
  • For regular users in production (e.g., user 49936), a downgrade immediately writes a row into cc_purchase and generates a PDF invoice via InvoiceHelper::prepareInvoiceData(), creating a phantom invoice in the database/UI even though Stripe/PayPal never billed any amount.

Proposed Changes

  1. app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Subscription/DowngradeHelper.php:

    • In insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade(), permanently remove/bypass the cc_purchase insertion ($this->paymentHelpers->insertTransaction()) and invoice generation ($this->invoiceHelper->prepareInvoiceData()) for all users.
    • Retain audit logging to cc_logs via $this->logDowngradeTransaction().
    • Always return ['link' => '', 'filename' => ''].
    • Deprecate/remove the unused $deferInvoice parameter.

  2. app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/Downgrade.php:

    • Remove deferInvoice: $this->isTestMode argument when calling insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade().

  3. app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/DowngradeHandler.php:

    • Remove deferInvoice: $this->isTestMode argument when calling insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade().

  4. Email Notification:

    • Verify sendDowngradeSuccessEmail() cleanly handles empty invoice links/filenames (already supported without errors).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Downgrading subscription via Stripe does not insert a new row in cc_purchase.
  • Downgrading subscription via Stripe does not generate an invoice PDF.
  • Downgrading subscription via PayPal does not insert a row in cc_purchase or generate invoice PDF.
  • Audit log entry in cc_logs is still created for all downgrade attempts.
  • Downgrade success email is sent without broken invoice links.
  • Plan schedule and pending downgrade state in DB remain functioning as expected.

Result

Permanently bypassed cc_purchase insertion and invoice PDF generation (prepareInvoiceData) for all subscription downgrades across Stripe and PayPal in DowngradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade(). The method always returns ['link' => '', 'filename' => ''] while preserving audit logging to cc_logs via logDowngradeTransaction(). Both Downgrade.php (Stripe) and DowngradeHandler.php (PayPal) were updated to remove the $deferInvoice argument. Added unit tests in DowngradeHelperTest.php covering both Stripe and PayPal downgrade flows to verify that cc_purchase insertion and invoice generation are never invoked, and verified manual testing on both payment gateways.

Merged via PR #1893 (commit 9496d50).

issues.display_title: Issue #1865: Create v2/tours/batch/archive API to delegate tour validation to background worker
issues.main_description_html:
Background & Problem:
v1/tours/batch/archive processes batch archive requests synchronously (DB queries + file checks per tour), blocking the response and causing timeouts on large batches.

Proposed Solution:
Introduce v2/tours/batch/archive that only gathers target moderation_ids and enqueues them; a background worker runs the heavy validations asynchronously.

Tasks / Acceptance Criteria:

  • v2/tours/batch/archive route + batchArchiveToursV2 controller (filtering ported from v1: user, tags, types, search)
  • Dispatch to new RabbitMQ queue v2_batch_archive_validation → fast 202 Accepted response
  • Validation worker: ownership → active overlay → pano check → published status; valid tours pushed to archivate_tour_space + sent_to_archive = '1'; failures logged + error emails, no requeue loops

Results (15 Sep 2026)

Merged via PR #1866; worker deployed via pm2 on apil-gothru-1 (www-data).

E2E verified on production data:

  • ✅ 202 Accepted fast response — local (prod config) & https://apil.gothru.co (1.0s)
  • ✅ Success (mid 3471027): queued → validated < 1s → archivate_tour_space → sent_to_archive=1 → archive completed (delete_space=1)
  • ✅ Failure cases: missing panos (log + notification email), non-owned mid, active overlay (DB untouched) — all acked, no requeue loops
  • ✅ Endpoint guards: 401 no token, 409 invalid type, 409 no tours found

issues.display_title: Issue #1884: fix(auth): revoke GT JWT on logout — write token_expired_ Redis denylist
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

LogoutAction deletes the sid session but never revokes the GT JWT. The Redis denylist key token_expired_<token> is read in checkToken() but no code anywhere writes it, so a logged-out token keeps working until its 30-day expiry.

Background

  • app/Class/HelperClass.php:238-252 — checkToken() checks the Redis denylist first, then decodes and compares exp.
  • app/Actions/Auth/LogoutAction.php — deletes the DB session + revokes Keycloak sessions via the Admin API, but does not touch the GT JWT.
  • GT tokens have ~30-day TTLs, so logout is currently advisory for API calls made with the Authorization header.

Tasks

  1. In LogoutAction, revoke the presented GT JWT: write token_expired_<token> to Redis with TTL = the token's remaining lifetime (so entries self-clean).
  2. Verify checkToken() reads the exact same key format (it already reads it — confirm key naming matches the writer).
  3. Review the Admin API revoke call (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{sub}/logout): it kills all Keycloak sessions for that user (every device). With the FE moving to the standard end-session endpoint (post_logout_redirect_uri + id_token_hint, GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4291), consider dropping this call or scoping it as fallback only, to avoid force-logging out the user's other devices.

Acceptance

  • Logout invalidates the current GT token immediately (subsequent API calls with it return 401)
  • Denylist entries auto-expire with the token TTL (no permanent growth)
  • Other devices are not force-logged-out unexpectedly once the per-session end-session flow is adopted

Result

Implemented in #1889 (open, awaiting merge).

  • GtTokenRevoker::revoke() — writes token_expired_<token> (the exact raw Authorization value keyed by checkToken()) with TTL = the token's remaining lifetime, so entries self-clean; best-effort (invalid tokens / Redis outages return false, never throw)
  • LogoutAction — invokes an injectable ?callable $revokeToken after session deletion; LogoutController passes the Authorization header into LogoutDto (the FE already sends it on every request)
  • Task 3 resolved with a decision: the Admin-API revoke (POST /admin/realms/.../users/{sub}/logout) was removed together with logoutUser()/getAdminAccessToken() (dead code, incl. the client_credentials admin-token usage). SSO session termination is now handled solely by the dashboard's end-session flow (GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4294); trade-off (logout from a tab without id_token does not end the SSO session) documented in the PR
  • Verification: auth suite 21/21 (incl. +3 revocation cases); the 2 Photographers/NotifyUpdateDtoTest failures are pre-existing on origin/main; docs/v2/auth/logout.md refreshed to match the new flow

issues.display_title: Issue #1885: fix(auth): validate azp/aud on POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

KeycloakTokenHelper::verifyAndGetClaims() validates only the RS256 signature and iss. Any access token signed by the realm's keys — issued to any client in the realm — is accepted. Add an azp/aud check against the expected dashboard client.

Background

  • app/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelper.php:32-48 — verifyAndGetClaims() compares iss to the realm issuer (when configured), then returns claims.
  • Token exchange happens after the FE migration to code flow + PKCE (GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4290); the FE sends its Keycloak access token to this endpoint to be swapped for a GT token.
  • Severity depends on the realm's client topology, but the check is cheap and closes the hole.

Tasks

  1. Add an allowed-client check: reject tokens whose azp (falling back to aud) is not the expected Keycloak client id (new env, e.g. KEYCLOAK_EXPECTED_CLIENT_ID, or reuse KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID).
  2. Keep fail-closed behavior when config is missing (consistent with the issuer check).
  3. While touching this area, document POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login in docs/v2/auth/ — it is missing from README.md today.

Acceptance

  • Access token from a different client in the realm → rejected (401)
  • Access token from the dashboard client → accepted
  • docs/v2/auth/ documents the keycloak-login endpoint

Result

Implemented in #1895 (open, awaiting merge).

  • KeycloakTokenHelper::validateClient() — validates token azp and aud claims against KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS, fallback KEYCLOAK_EXPECTED_CLIENT_ID, default 'gothru-dashboard'. Supports comma-separated list and * wildcard. Throws InvalidTokenException (401) on untrusted client.
  • tests/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelperTest.php (6/6 tests pass) — covers default dashboard client, allowed clients list, aud fallback, aud array, wildcard, and rejection.
  • docs/v2/auth/keycloak-login.md — comprehensive documentation for POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login added and linked in README.md.
  • Verification: tests/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelperTest.php (6/6) and tests/Actions/Auth (21/21) pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #1894: feat(auth): auto-register (JIT provision) new users on Keycloak login
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Support auto-registration / JIT (Just-In-Time) user provisioning when logging in via Keycloak if the user does not exist in the database yet, matching the existing Google OAuth registration flow (LoginGoogle & RegisterGoogle).

Background

Currently, KeycloakLoginAction::resolveUser() only searches for an existing user by keycloak_sub or email. If no matching record is found in users, it throws UserNotFoundException (which maps to 409).
As noted in KeycloakLoginAction.php:27:

/**
 * Resolves the Keycloak identity to an existing GoThru user, then issues
 * the GT token. Registration (JIT provisioning) is handled separately.
 */

In contrast, Google login (app/Http/Controllers/Auth/Actions/LoginGoogle.php:80-86) checks if the user exists; if not, it automatically registers the user via RegisterGoogle::execute($dataEmail, $googleId, $dataGoogle) and proceeds with session creation.

Reference: Google Registration Flow (RegisterGoogle.php)

When a new Google user logs in:

  1. Inserts into users table:
    • user_name: email or username
    • email: email from Google
    • first_name & last_name from profile
    • google_id: Google sub ID
    • date_created: current timestamp
    • is_active: '1' & verified_email: '1'
  2. Inserts into user_extra_data:
    • user_id: created ID
    • newsletter: '0'
    • is_new: 'Y'
  3. Creates user storage directory:
    • /data/moderation/{userId}
  4. Generates RSS resources:
    • RssClass::addRSS($userId)
    • RssClass::createRssFeed($rssKey)
  5. Logs activity via ElasticLogClass::addLog(['action' => 'register_user'])
  6. If an existing user was found with is_active == 0, activates the account (is_active = 1, verified_email = 1).

Tasks

  1. Create a dedicated handler or action (e.g. RegisterKeycloak or injectable provisioning service) following ADR and repository patterns.
  2. In KeycloakLoginAction, when resolveUser() does not find an existing user by sub or email, call the register handler using claims extracted from Keycloak (sub, email, user_name, first_name, last_name).
  3. Set keycloak_sub on the newly created user record, with is_active = 1 and verified_email = 1.
  4. Initialize user_extra_data, /data/moderation/{userId} folder, RSS feed, and register log.
  5. If user exists with is_active == 0, reactivate and verify email (matching LoginGoogle).
  6. Issue GT JWT and session cookie as part of the unified login flow without throwing UserNotFoundException.
  7. Add unit tests in tests/Actions/Auth/KeycloakLoginActionTest.php covering auto-registration on first login.

Acceptance

  • New user logging in via Keycloak has their account automatically provisioned in users and user_extra_data
  • Directory /data/moderation/{userId} and RSS feed are created for the new user
  • Existing unverified/inactive user logging in via Keycloak is activated
  • Login completes successfully with GT JWT (gt.<token>) and session cookie
  • Unit tests pass

Result

Implemented in #1896 (open, awaiting merge).

  • KeycloakUserRegistrar (new) — provisions new user in users (keycloak_sub, is_active = 1, verified_email = 1), initializes user_extra_data, /data/moderation/{userId} folder, user RSS feed, and register log (matching Google OAuth flow).
  • KeycloakLoginAction — auto-registers non-existing users via injectable registrar instead of throwing UserNotFoundException (409); auto-activates inactive/unverified accounts on login.
  • AuthSessionRepository — added activateUser(int $userId).
  • KeycloakLoginActionTest — added unit tests for auto-registration and reactivation.
  • Verification: tests/Actions/Auth suite passes (22/22 pass, incl. 6/6 KeycloakLoginActionTest).

issues.display_title: Issue #1892: feat(photographers): forward client public IP via X-Real-IP header to photographer backend
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Forward the client's public IP address from GoThru API callers to the upstream Photographer API (BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER) via the X-Real-IP HTTP request header.

Background

The Photographer backend requires the original public IP of the user/client making requests rather than the internal IP of the GoThru API server or intermediary proxies.

Requirements

  • Automatically resolve the public IP of incoming requests using standard proxy precedence:
    1. CF-Connecting-IP (Cloudflare)
    2. X-Forwarded-For (first IP in chain)
    3. X-Real-IP (Reverse proxy / Nginx)
    4. $request->ip() (Lumen/Laravel default)
  • Attach the X-Real-IP HTTP header on all outbound HTTP requests made to BASE_URL_PHOTOGRAPHER.
  • Cover all Photographer services and endpoints:
    • ProfileService
    • PortfolioService
    • PhotographerServicesService
    • ProfessionalServicesService
    • AvailabilityService
    • ToolService
    • ReviewService
    • PhotographerSupportService
    • Legacy action controllers under Portfolio/Action/, Services/Action/, Availabilities/Action/

Implementation & PRs

  • PR #1890: Initial implementation on GET /photographers/profile with ClientIpHelper.
  • PR #1891: Full rollout across all photographer services and endpoints.
